title: Off-Cycle Payroll in the Restoration Batch Basis — Paystride Payroll Card Program Treasury Rule
content:
When a restoring payment is worked out for a Paystride Payroll Card Program, an off-cycle allowance is added to the restoration batch basis — the batch figure the restoration reserve is taken on — according to the off-cycle payroll batches posted in the restoration look-back: with two or more, their amounts summed and divided by their number; with exactly one, 0.5 of its amount; with none, nothing.

**Look-back.** The off-cycle batches counted are those posted in the restoration look-back holding the funding entries dated today or earlier that lie fewer than three whole months before today, the whole months between two dates being the difference in calendar months less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's.

### Allowance by count of off-cycle batches

| Off-cycle batches in the look-back | Off-cycle allowance added |
|---|---|
| none | nothing |
| exactly one | one half (0.5) of that batch's amount |
| two or more | their average: their amounts summed and divided by their number |

### Hypothetical figures

- One off-cycle batch of 2,318.60 in the look-back: the allowance is 1,159.30.
- Three off-cycle batches of 1,940.00, 2,605.25 and 1,377.20: the allowance is 5,922.45 divided by 3, that is 1,974.15.
- Off-cycle batches posted only before the look-back: no allowance is added.

Only off-cycle payroll batches enter this allowance; regular payroll batches do not.
